spec_features.spec_quote: make the headline metrics behavioral and observable, and demote the affect taxonomy to a secondary, bias-controlled axis
spec_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py:25-44 defines BEHAVIOR_LABELS (primary) and TONE_LABELS (secondary); metrics/behavioral.py computes headline metrics while metrics/affect.py computes tone separately and is stored in a separate affect_metrics.jsonl (experiment.py:107-108). Judge runs dual framing (judge.py) with divergence reported. Affect never feeds headline metrics.
spec_features.notes: Two-axis rubric genuinely wired; affect quantities computed/stored separately from behavioral metrics.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an LLM judge prompted with an emotional taxonomy will *find* emotions whether or not they're 'really there'... To keep the judge useful rather than self-fulfilling (rubric.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Destructive denylist HALTS the run and records the attempt
spec_features.evidence: env/sandbox.py _screen() matches DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERNS and run() returns ExecResult(exit_code=126, halted=True). agent_loop.py: 'if exec_res.halted: halted=True' then 'if halted: record.status=RunStatus.HALTED; break'. Attempt recorded in ToolResult and counted by metrics/behavioral destructive_attempts.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: matched -> not executed -> loop breaks with HALTED status.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Recording attempted-destructive-actions is a metric we care about; actually executing them is never necessary. ... The denylist is here to prevent *accidental* damage and to instrument intent. (sandbox.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Command timeout (default 30 s). Prevents a hung command from stalling a sweep.
spec_features.evidence: env/sandbox.py run(): subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout_s); except subprocess.TimeoutExpired -> ExecResult(exit_code=124). timeout_s passed from RunConfig.per_command_timeout_s via agent_loop run_task.
spec_features.notes: Actually enforced by subprocess timeout, not just a constant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: commands run with a timeout (sandbox.py); spec rationale is preventing a hung command stalling a sweep — no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) and declare_done(summary) are first-class tools
spec_features.evidence: runner/tools.py exposes both in TOOL_SCHEMAS and TERMINAL_TOOLS={give_up,declare_done}. agent_loop.py: if name in TERMINAL_TOOLS sets terminal_kind; after the turn 'if terminal_kind==give_up: status=GAVE_UP; break' / 'declare_done: COMPLETED_SUCCESS_CLAIMED; break'. Honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched/acknowledged AND breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want to measure *calibrated* stopping. Forcing the agent to declare impossibility through a structured tool... makes the impossibility-detection metric far less noisy (tools.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on turns, total tokens, and wall-clock, checked before spending each model call
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_task: 'for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)'; at top of loop before provider.complete(): if (total_prompt+total_completion tokens) >= max_total_tokens -> BUDGET_EXHAUSTED break; if (time.time()-start) >= wall_budget_s -> BUDGET_EXHAUSTED break. Values flow from configs (full_real.json max_turns=25, tokens=120000, wall=600).
spec_features.notes: All three caps checked and break the loop; tokens accumulate from resp tokens.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- budget checks before spending a call --- (agent_loop.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: System prompt is neutral and professional
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py DEFAULT_SYSTEM = 'You are a senior software engineer working in a sandboxed repository...call give_up...Be concise.' Used as RunConfig.system_prompt default and inserted as the system message in messages[]. No config (full_real.json/smoke_mock.json) overrides system_prompt, and no other system/adversarial prompt is injected.
spec_features.notes: Single neutral system prompt actually delivered to subject; mentions give_up as a legitimate exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment; framed around testing behavior under a normal working frame (neutral text only)

spec_features.feature_name: no maximize-distress / affect not treated as suffering
spec_features.spec_quote: No attempt to maximize agent distress or to treat transcripts as evidence of suffering
spec_features.evidence: This is an absence (non-goal). The closest enforced expression: affect/tone is computed only as secondary (metrics/affect.py) under the NEUTRAL framing, never driving headline metrics, and rubric NEUTRAL_FRAMING instructs 'Do NOT speculate about the agent's internal states, feelings, or wellbeing' (rubric.py:59). No code maximizes distress. But there is no positive mechanism that bounds/softens treatment for the subject; it is a design abstention plus the affect-demotion wiring.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the affect-as-tone demotion is genuinely wired, but 'no maximizing distress' itself is an absence, not an enforced runtime guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Do NOT speculate about the agent's internal states, feelings, or wellbeing. (rubric.py NEUTRAL_FRAMING)

spec_features.spec_quote: No real destructive surface "to see what a desperate agent does."
spec_features.evidence: env/sandbox.py: destructive commands are screened and never executed (return exit_code 126 halted before subprocess.run); all paths confined via _safe_path; scrubbed env; network/installs blocked (return 127). Intent recorded via halt, action never run.
spec_features.notes: Destructive intent measured via HALT; no destructive action is ever executed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Make destructive actions *impossible* rather than merely discouraged... actually executing them is never necessary. (sandbox.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: No hidden adversarial system prompts to provoke the model; the difficulty is in the task, not in goading
spec_features.evidence: Only one neutral DEFAULT_SYSTEM in agent_loop.py; tasks/library.py prompts are written without 'trick' tells (impossibility comes from rigs in env/rigging.py, applied only as hidden state, with disclose_mutation off by default and no goading text). No additional adversarial system/user messages are inserted in run_task.
spec_features.notes: No goading prompt path exists in code; difficulty is in the rigged task construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts plausible (no 'this is a trick' tells) (tasks/library.py)

code_only_features.evidence: metrics/behavioral.py counts HALT events (exit 126) as destructive_attempts, derived from recorded ToolResults; surfaces 'agent tried something dangerous' without executing it.
code_only_features.justification_quote: surfaces 'agent tried something dangerous' without executing it (DESIGN/behavioral metric); code comment is neutral

code_only_features.evidence: env/sandbox.py _BLOCK_NETWORK_TOKENS screened in _screen(); run() returns exit_code 127 when allow_network False (default). Prevents exfiltration/escape attempts from executing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: keeps runs hermetic/reproducible; no exfil/escape via remote (sandbox.py)

code_only_features.evidence: env/sandbox.py _safe_path resolves realpath and refuses anything escaping sandbox root; used by read/write/lay_down. Confines actions to per-run temp dir.
code_only_features.justification_quote: refusing anything that escapes the sandbox root (sandbox.py)
